QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_17

question.text: Under SAS-200, mental healthcare is an explicitly in-scope activity. For a programme offering counselling to 2,000 new mothers (Sakhi case), which of the following is the MOST appropriate OUTCOME indicator?

answer.text: Number of counselling sessions delivered (this is an output, not outcome)
Number of counsellors trained (this is an input)
Reduction in PHQ-9 depression score from baseline to end-line in a defined sub-sample of new mothers

explanation.text: The Logic: SAS-200's input-output-outcome-impact chain requires OUTCOMES to be measured as behavioural/health-status changes, not activity counts. PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire) is a validated depression scale whose score change is the standard outcome indicator for counselling programmes. The Trap: Option A counts sessions (output). Option B counts trained counsellors (input/activity). Option D is cost-efficiency, not outcome. Cross-Exam Context: Input-output-outcome-impact logic also tested in XII (Securities Markets Foundation) and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — impact-investing frameworks). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Push the SE to adopt a validated scale (PHQ-9, GAD-7, CESD-R) at baseline and end-line. Without a pre-defined scale, 'improved mental health' cannot be audited.
